subject: English
summaryPoints: Direct speech transforms to reported speech via tense backshifting when the reporting verb is in the past: simple present shifts to simple past, simple past and present perfect shift to past perfect, will shifts to would, and can shifts to could.

Deictic adverbs and demonstratives change perspective in reported speech: 'this/these' -> 'that/those', 'here' -> 'there', 'now' -> 'then', 'today' -> 'that day', 'yesterday' -> 'the day before/the previous day', and 'tomorrow' -> 'the next/following day'.

Vague and ambiguous pronoun references impair sentence clarity: ambiguous reference occurs when a pronoun can refer to multiple possible antecedents, remote reference occurs when the antecedent is too distant, and vague reference occurs when the pronoun refers to an unstated idea.

Formal debate follows a structured procedure: affirmative team arguments, opposing team counter-arguments, and subsequent rebuttals, judged on Manner (delivery/gestures), Matter (content/evidence), and Method (organization/structure).
Punctuation conventions for direct speech require enclosing spoken words in quotation marks, setting off dialogue tags with commas, and placing commas or periods inside closing quotation marks.
Phrasal verbs based on 'look' and 'run' include 'look back on' (reminisce), 'look forward to' (anticipate with pleasure), 'run out of' (exhaust supply), and 'put up with' (tolerate).

formulas.label: Reported Speech Tense Shift Hierarchy
formulas.expr: V1 -> V2  |  V2 / has/have + V3 -> had + V3  |  am/is/are -> was/were  |  will / can -> would / could

formulas.label: Deictic Time & Space Conversions
formulas.expr: now -> then  |  today -> that day  |  yesterday -> the previous day  |  tomorrow -> the following day  |  here -> there

formulas.label: Direct Speech Quotation Punctuation
formulas.expr: "Spoken statement," + reporting clause.  OR  Reporting clause + , + "Spoken statement."

formulas.label: Ambiguous Pronoun Reference Resolution
formulas.expr: Ambiguous: Hanan told Sara that she won.  ->  Clear: Hanan told Sara, "You won."  OR  Hanan informed Sara of Hanan's victory.

examTip: In EUEE reported speech items, remember that simple past (V2) backshifts to past perfect ('had + V3'); it does not remain simple past when the reporting verb is in the past. In vague pronoun items, watch out for pronouns like 'they' or 'it' used without clear antecedents (e.g., 'At the hospital, they said...' is vague; correct to 'The doctors at the hospital said...').

keyDefinitions.definition: A syntactic transformation reporting another person's utterance without quoting words verbatim, using tense backshifting, pronoun adjustments, and deictic shifts.
A grammatical fault in which a pronoun could refer to more than one preceding noun antecedent, rendering the intended meaning uncertain.
An error occurring when a pronoun refers to an entire implied idea or unmentioned entity rather than to a specific, stated noun antecedent.
A formal competitive discussion where affirmative and opposing teams defend or refute a predetermined resolution governed by strict time limits and rebuttal rules.

eueeFocusTopics: Tense backshifting rules and time/place deictic conversions in reported speech
Identifying and correcting ambiguous, remote, and vague pronoun references
Punctuation mechanics for direct speech quotations, commas, and dialogue tags
Three pillars of formal debate: Manner, Matter, and Method
Three-word phrasal verbs ('look forward to', 'run out of', 'put up with')
